chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Butyne is treated with 1. NaNH2; 2. 1-Bromopropane?
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Butyne with 1. NaNH2; 2. 1-Bromopropane yields 3-Heptyne + NaBr. Rationale: Acetylide anion acts as a strong nucleophile, displacing bromide in an SN2 reaction to lengthen the carbon chain.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Hexyne into 2-Hexanone?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Hexyne into 2-Hexanone, the appropriate reagent is H2O, H2SO4, HgSO4. Rationale: Markovnikov addition of water produces an enol that tautomerizes to the methyl ketone.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Hexyne is treated with 1. Disiamylborane; 2. H2O2, NaOH?
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Hexyne with 1. Disiamylborane; 2. H2O2, NaOH yields Hexanal. Rationale: Bulky borane adds to the terminal carbon, producing an aldehyde upon basic peroxide oxidation.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Pentyne into cis-2-Pentene?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Pentyne into cis-2-Pentene, the appropriate reagent is H2 / Lindlar catalyst. Rationale: Poisoned palladium catalyst allows syn-hydrogenation of alkyne to cis-alkene without further reduction.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Pentyne is treated with Na / liquid NH3 (-78°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Pentyne with Na / liquid NH3 (-78°C) yields trans-2-Pentene. Rationale: Stepwise electron and proton transfer through a trans-radical anion intermediate yields the trans-alkene.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Pentyne into Pentane?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Pentyne into Pentane, the appropriate reagent is Excess H2 / Pt. Rationale: Unpoisoned platinum catalyst reduces alkynes completely through alkene to alkane.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1 equivalent Br2 in CH2Cl2 to yield (E)-2,3-Dibromo-2-butene as the major product?
questions.explanation: 2-Butyne reacts with 1 equivalent Br2 in CH2Cl2 to yield (E)-2,3-Dibromo-2-butene. Rationale: Anti-addition of one equivalent of bromine across the triple bond yields the trans-dibromoalkene.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1,2-Dibromobutane is treated with 2 equivalents NaNH2 / mineral oil (150°C)?
questions.explanation: Treating 1,2-Dibromobutane with 2 equivalents NaNH2 / mineral oil (150°C) yields 1-Butyne. Rationale: Two successive E2 eliminations convert the vicinal dibromide into a carbon-carbon triple bond.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. O3; 2. H2O to yield Acetic acid + Propanoic acid as the major product?
questions.explanation: 2-Pentyne reacts with 1. O3; 2. H2O to yield Acetic acid + Propanoic acid. Rationale: Ozonolysis cleaves the internal triple bond, converting both alkyne carbons into carboxylic acids.

questions.chapter_title: Alkynes: An Introduction to Organic Synthesis
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Pentyne is treated with KMnO4 / H2O (neutral)?
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Pentyne with KMnO4 / H2O (neutral) yields Butanoic acid + CO2. Rationale: Oxidative cleavage of a terminal alkyne yields a carboxylic acid from the internal carbon and CO2 from terminal carbon.
